pages.text: Hot sun shines over sandy dunes. Cami the camel steps forward, her wide feet pressing softly without sinking.
Sand blows in the wind, but Cami’s long eyelashes help keep gritty dust out of her eyes.
Her hump stands tall. A camel’s hump stores fat, which is energy the body can use later.
Because deserts are dry, Cami can travel a long time without water when she needs to.
At an oasis, Cami drinks a lot quickly. Camels can drink big gulps when water is available.
Wide feet act like snowshoes on sand. They spread weight and help Cami walk on soft dunes.
Cami’s nose can close a bit during dusty winds. That helps keep sand out while she walks.
In the cooler evening, Cami continues her journey. Many desert animals move more when it is less hot.
Cami meets people traveling too. For many places, camels are helpful for carrying loads across deserts.
Bedtime thought: camels use smart body tools—humps, eyelashes, and wide feet—to live in dry, windy deserts.
